parameters.content:
## B1 · The Optimization Treasure Hunt
**Stage 0** · Nova Pro compiles each product's free-text criteria ONCE into checkable rules (cached by text hash) → LLM cost scales with distinct criteria texts, not users.
**Stage 1+2** · SQL equivalence classes: every threshold is a cut point, users with identical intervals form one class → decide class x product.
**Stage 3** · expand to users, fit score, diff vs active matches (one transaction, advisory lock).
**Proof** · naive per-user re-evaluation must give 0 mismatches.

parameters.query:
SELECT DISTINCT encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') AS text_id,
       p.other_criteria_text AS text
FROM loan_products p
WHERE p.is_active AND p.other_criteria_text IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM criteria_rules r
                  WHERE r.prompt_version = $1
                    AND r.criteria_text_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex'))
ORDER BY 1

WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO criteria_rules (criteria_text_hash, prompt_version, rules, requirements, model_id,
                              llm_input_tokens, llm_output_tokens)
  SELECT criteria_text_hash, prompt_version, rules, requirements, model_id, NULL, NULL
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset($2::jsonb) AS r(criteria_text_hash text, prompt_version text, rules jsonb,
                                          requirements jsonb, model_id text)
  ON CONFLICT (criteria_text_hash, prompt_version) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING 1
)
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET rules_compiled = (SELECT count(*) FROM ins), llm_calls = $3::int,
       llm_input_tokens = $4::int, llm_output_tokens = $5::int, llm_cost_usd_est = $6::numeric
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING rules_compiled, llm_calls

-- Workflow B · Stage 1 + 2: exact equivalence classes, then a decision per class x product.
-- Params: $1 run_id (uuid text), $2 prompt_version of the compiled residual rules.
--
-- Idea: every threshold any in-scope product uses (its hard criteria AND the numbers in
-- its LLM-compiled residual rules) is a CUT POINT. Two users whose income, credit score
-- and age fall between the same consecutive cut points, with the same employment type,
-- get identical answers to every rule, so they form one class. We decide once per
-- class x product and expand to users later. Exact, not banded: no false positives.
--
-- Why floors are exact: for any cut c, value >= c  <=>  floor(value) >= c, where
-- floor(value) = the largest cut <= value (or -1 below all cuts). So every comparison
-- against a cut gives the same answer on the floor as on the real value.
WITH run AS (
    SELECT * FROM pipeline_runs WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
), prods AS (
    SELECT p.*, r.rules AS residual_rules, r.requirements AS residual_requirements
    FROM loan_products p
    LEFT JOIN criteria_rules r
           ON r.prompt_version = $2
          AND r.criteria_text_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex')
    WHERE p.is_active
      AND ((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'upload' OR p.product_id = ANY (coalesce((SELECT scope_product_ids FROM run), ARRAY[]::uuid[])))
), usr AS (
    SELECT u.* FROM users u
    WHERE (SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products' OR u.upload_job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
), rule_values AS (  -- numbers inside the compiled residual rules are cut points too
    SELECT x->>'field' AS field, x->>'op' AS op, (x->>'value')::numeric AS v
    FROM prods, jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(residual_rules, '[]'::jsonb)) AS x
), cuts AS (
    -- ">= v" splits at ceil(v); "<= v" splits at floor(v) + 1 (integer fields)
    SELECT 'income' AS dim, min_monthly_income AS c FROM prods WHERE min_monthly_income IS NOT NULL
    UNION SELECT 'income', ceil(v)::int FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'monthly_income' AND op = '>='
    UNION SELECT 'income', floor(v)::int + 1 FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'monthly_income' AND op = '<='
    UNION SELECT 'score', min_credit_score FROM prods WHERE min_credit_score IS NOT NULL
    UNION SELECT 'score', max_credit_score + 1 FROM prods WHERE max_credit_score IS NOT NULL
    UNION SELECT 'score', ceil(v)::int FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'credit_score' AND op = '>='
    UNION SELECT 'score', floor(v)::int + 1 FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'credit_score' AND op = '<='
    UNION SELECT 'age', min_age FROM prods WHERE min_age IS NOT NULL
    UNION SELECT 'age', max_age + 1 FROM prods WHERE max_age IS NOT NULL
    UNION SELECT 'age', ceil(v)::int FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'age' AND op = '>='
    UNION SELECT 'age', floor(v)::int + 1 FROM rule_values WHERE field = 'age' AND op = '<='
), user_floors AS (
    SELECT u.user_id, u.employment_status,
        coalesce((SELECT max(c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'income' AND c <= u.monthly_income), -1) AS income_floor,
        coalesce((SELECT max(c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'score' AND c <= u.credit_score), -1) AS score_floor,
        coalesce((SELECT max(c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'age' AND c <= u.age), -1) AS age_floor
    FROM usr u
), classes AS (
    SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY employment_status, income_floor, score_floor, age_floor)::int AS class_id,
           income_floor, score_floor, age_floor, employment_status, count(*)::int AS users
    FROM user_floors
    GROUP BY employment_status, income_floor, score_floor, age_floor
), pairs AS (  -- Stage 1: hard criteria (NULL = "lender states no limit" = passes)
    SELECT c.class_id, c.users, c.income_floor, c.score_floor, c.age_floor, c.employment_status,
           p.product_id, p.other_criteria_text, p.verification, p.residual_rules, p.residual_requirements
    FROM classes c
    JOIN prods p ON
         (p.min_monthly_income IS NULL OR c.income_floor >= p.min_monthly_income)
     AND (p.min_credit_score   IS NULL OR c.score_floor  >= p.min_credit_score)
     AND (p.max_credit_score   IS NULL OR c.score_floor  <  p.max_credit_score + 1)
     AND (p.min_age            IS NULL OR c.age_floor    >= p.min_age)
     AND (p.max_age            IS NULL OR c.age_floor    <  p.max_age + 1)
     AND (p.employment_types   IS NULL OR c.employment_status = ANY (p.employment_types))
), judged AS (  -- Stage 2: the compiled residual rules, evaluated on the class floors
    SELECT pr.*,
        (SELECT coalesce(bool_and(CASE
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN pr.income_floor >= ceil((x->>'value')::numeric)
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN pr.income_floor <  floor((x->>'value')::numeric) + 1
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN pr.score_floor  >= ceil((x->>'value')::numeric)
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN pr.score_floor  <  floor((x->>'value')::numeric) + 1
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN pr.age_floor    >= ceil((x->>'value')::numeric)
                    WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN pr.age_floor    <  floor((x->>'value')::numeric) + 1
                    ELSE true END), true)
         FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(pr.residual_rules, '[]'::jsonb)) AS x
         WHERE x->>'applies_to' IN ('any', pr.employment_status)) AS rules_pass
    FROM pairs pr
), decided AS (
    SELECT class_id, users, product_id,
        CASE
            WHEN other_criteria_text IS NULL                  THEN 'eligible'     -- nothing left to check
            WHEN residual_rules IS NULL                       THEN 'conditional'  -- not compiled / unverified: never a rejection
            WHEN NOT rules_pass                               THEN 'not_eligible'
            WHEN jsonb_array_length(residual_requirements) > 0 THEN 'conditional'
            ELSE 'eligible' END AS tier,
        CASE
            WHEN other_criteria_text IS NULL THEN 'sql'
            WHEN residual_rules IS NULL      THEN 'rules'
            ELSE 'llm_rules' END AS stage,
        CASE
            WHEN other_criteria_text IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN residual_rules IS NULL      THEN other_criteria_text
            ELSE nullif(array_to_string(ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(residual_requirements)), '; '), '')
        END AS requirements
    FROM judged
), ins_classes AS (
    INSERT INTO match_classes (run_id, class_id, income_floor, score_floor, age_floor, employment_status, users)
    SELECT $1::uuid, class_id, income_floor, score_floor, age_floor, employment_status, users FROM classes
    RETURNING 1
), ins_pairs AS (
    INSERT INTO match_pairs (run_id, class_id, product_id, tier, stage, requirements)
    SELECT $1::uuid, class_id, product_id, tier, stage, requirements FROM decided
    RETURNING 1
)
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET
    users_in            = (SELECT count(*) FROM usr),
    products_in         = (SELECT count(*) FROM prods),
    naive_pairs         = (SELECT count(*) FROM usr) * (SELECT count(*) FROM prods),
    classes             = (SELECT count(*) FROM classes),
    class_product_pairs = (SELECT count(*) FROM classes) * (SELECT count(*) FROM prods),
    pairs_after_sql     = (SELECT coalesce(sum(users), 0) FROM pairs),
    rule_decided        = (SELECT count(*) FROM decided WHERE stage IN ('sql', 'rules')),
    llm_candidates      = (SELECT count(*) FROM decided WHERE stage = 'llm_rules'),
    not_eligible_pairs  = (SELECT count(*) FROM decided WHERE tier = 'not_eligible'),
    residual_texts      = (SELECT count(DISTINCT other_criteria_text) FROM prods),
    -- coalesce: a dimension with no thresholds (e.g. a product-mode run whose product has no
    -- age rule) must be stored as [] - jsonb_agg of zero rows is NULL -> JSON null, and Stage 3
    -- cannot iterate a scalar (found by the product-mode integration test).
    cuts = jsonb_build_object(
        'income', coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(c ORDER BY c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'income'), '[]'::jsonb),
        'score',  coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(c ORDER BY c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'score'), '[]'::jsonb),
        'age',    coalesce((SELECT jsonb_agg(c ORDER BY c) FROM cuts WHERE dim = 'age'), '[]'::jsonb)),
    -- Reference the data-modifying CTEs so they are part of this statement.
    error = CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM ins_classes) >= 0 AND (SELECT count(*) FROM ins_pairs) >= 0
                 THEN NULL END
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id, mode, users_in, products_in, naive_pairs, classes, class_product_pairs,
          pairs_after_sql, rule_decided, llm_candidates, not_eligible_pairs, residual_texts, cuts;

-- Workflow B · between Stage 1 and Stage 3: refresh planner statistics.
-- Stage 1 just bulk-wrote match_classes/match_pairs and earlier runs wrote matches; with
-- stale statistics Postgres estimated ~26 rows instead of ~272,000 and picked nested-loop
-- joins (a 7-minute Stage 3 in testing). ANALYZE takes about a second and fixes the plan.
-- Allowed for n8n_workflows by GRANT MAINTAIN (PostgreSQL 17) on exactly these tables.
ANALYZE match_classes, match_pairs, matches;

-- Workflow B · Stage 3: expand class decisions to users, score fit, diff against active
-- matches. ONE statement = one transaction, serialized by an advisory lock so an
-- upload-mode run and a product-mode run can never create duplicate active pairs.
-- Params: $1 run_id.
--
-- Fit score (0-100, transparent, every term traceable to a published lender rule):
--   tier            eligible 60 | conditional 35
--   income headroom up to 15  (user income / lender minimum: 1x -> 0, 3x or more -> 15)
--   credit margin   up to 10  (points above the lender minimum, capped at +100)
--   interest rate   up to 15  (lower starting rate is better; 0% -> 15, 30%+ -> 0)
--   unknown criterion -> half credit (neither rewarded nor punished)
WITH lck AS (
    SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(424242) AS locked
), run AS (
    SELECT r.* FROM pipeline_runs r, lck WHERE r.run_id = $1::uuid
), usr AS (
    SELECT u.* FROM users u
    WHERE (SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products' OR u.upload_job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
), user_class AS (  -- the same floors Stage 1 used (cuts stored on the run)
    SELECT u.user_id, u.monthly_income, u.credit_score, mc.class_id
    FROM usr u
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT coalesce((SELECT max(c::int) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text((SELECT cuts->'income' FROM run)) c WHERE c::int <= u.monthly_income), -1) AS fi,
               coalesce((SELECT max(c::int) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text((SELECT cuts->'score' FROM run)) c WHERE c::int <= u.credit_score), -1) AS fs,
               coalesce((SELECT max(c::int) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text((SELECT cuts->'age' FROM run)) c WHERE c::int <= u.age), -1) AS fa
    ) f
    JOIN match_classes mc ON mc.run_id = $1::uuid AND mc.income_floor = f.fi AND mc.score_floor = f.fs
                         AND mc.age_floor = f.fa AND mc.employment_status = u.employment_status
), scored AS (
    SELECT uc.user_id, mp.product_id, mp.tier, mp.requirements,
        CASE mp.stage WHEN 'llm_rules' THEN 'llm' ELSE mp.stage END AS stage_decided,
        round(
              CASE mp.tier WHEN 'eligible' THEN 60 ELSE 35 END
            + 15 * CASE WHEN p.min_monthly_income IS NULL THEN 0.5
                        ELSE least(greatest(uc.monthly_income::numeric / p.min_monthly_income - 1, 0), 2) / 2 END
            + 10 * CASE WHEN p.min_credit_score IS NULL THEN 0.5
                        ELSE least(greatest(uc.credit_score - p.min_credit_score, 0), 100) / 100.0 END
            + 15 * CASE WHEN p.interest_rate_min IS NULL THEN 0.5
                        ELSE greatest(30 - least(p.interest_rate_min, 30), 0) / 30.0 END
        , 1) AS fit_score,
        jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
            'income_multiple', round(uc.monthly_income::numeric / nullif(p.min_monthly_income, 0), 1),
            'credit_margin',   uc.credit_score - p.min_credit_score,
            'rate_from',       p.interest_rate_min,
            'has_conditions',  mp.requirements IS NOT NULL)) AS fit_reasons
    FROM user_class uc
    JOIN match_pairs mp ON mp.run_id = $1::uuid AND mp.class_id = uc.class_id
                       AND mp.tier IN ('eligible', 'conditional')
    JOIN loan_products p ON p.product_id = mp.product_id
), current_active AS (  -- active matches inside this run's scope
    SELECT m.match_id, m.user_id, m.product_id
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.status = 'active'
      AND (((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'upload' AND m.user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM usr))
        OR ((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products' AND m.product_id = ANY (coalesce((SELECT scope_product_ids FROM run), ARRAY[]::uuid[]))))
), ins AS (
    INSERT INTO matches (user_id, product_id, job_id, match_run_id, tier, requirements,
                         stage_decided, fit_score, fit_reasons)
    SELECT s.user_id, s.product_id, (SELECT job_id FROM run), $1::uuid, s.tier, s.requirements,
           s.stage_decided, s.fit_score, s.fit_reasons
    FROM scored s
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM current_active c WHERE c.user_id = s.user_id AND c.product_id = s.product_id)
    ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) WHERE status = 'active' DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
), upd AS (  -- tier/requirements changed on a pair the user already had: update in place, no new email
    UPDATE matches m SET tier = s.tier, requirements = s.requirements, fit_score = s.fit_score,
                         fit_reasons = s.fit_reasons, stage_decided = s.stage_decided
    FROM scored s
    WHERE m.status = 'active' AND m.user_id = s.user_id AND m.product_id = s.product_id
      AND (m.tier, m.requirements) IS DISTINCT FROM (s.tier, s.requirements)
    RETURNING 1
), sup AS (  -- no longer eligible: keep the history, mark superseded (no email)
    UPDATE matches m SET status = 'superseded', superseded_at = now()
    FROM current_active c
    WHERE m.match_id = c.match_id
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scored s WHERE s.user_id = c.user_id AND s.product_id = c.product_id)
    RETURNING 1
), job AS (
    UPDATE upload_jobs SET match_status = 'DONE', matched_at = now()
    WHERE job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
    RETURNING 1
)
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET
    matches_new        = (SELECT count(*) FROM ins),
    matches_superseded = (SELECT count(*) FROM sup),
    matches_unchanged  = (SELECT count(*) FROM scored) - (SELECT count(*) FROM ins) - (SELECT count(*) FROM upd),
    finished_at        = now(),
    error = CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM job) >= 0 THEN error END
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id, mode, job_id, matches_new, matches_superseded, matches_unchanged,
          (SELECT count(*) FROM upd) AS matches_updated, (SELECT count(*) FROM scored) AS matched_pairs;

-- Correctness proof for the Treasure Hunt (PLAN.md §11.9).
-- Params: $1 run_id, $2 prompt_version.
--
-- Re-decides EVERY user x product pair the naive way: real values, no classes, no floors,
-- one row per pair. Then compares with what the optimized pipeline produced (class
-- decisions expanded to users). The optimization is correct iff the two sets are identical.
WITH run AS (
    SELECT * FROM pipeline_runs WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
), prods AS (
    SELECT p.*, r.rules AS residual_rules, r.requirements AS residual_requirements
    FROM loan_products p
    LEFT JOIN criteria_rules r
           ON r.prompt_version = $2
          AND r.criteria_text_hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(p.other_criteria_text, 'UTF8')), 'hex')
    WHERE p.is_active
      AND ((SELECT mode FROM run) = 'upload' OR p.product_id = ANY (coalesce((SELECT scope_product_ids FROM run), ARRAY[]::uuid[])))
), usr AS (
    SELECT u.* FROM users u
    WHERE (SELECT mode FROM run) = 'products' OR u.upload_job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM run)
), naive AS (  -- every user x every product, decided on the user's REAL values
    SELECT u.user_id, p.product_id,
        CASE
            WHEN NOT ((p.min_monthly_income IS NULL OR u.monthly_income >= p.min_monthly_income)
                  AND (p.min_credit_score   IS NULL OR u.credit_score  >= p.min_credit_score)
                  AND (p.max_credit_score   IS NULL OR u.credit_score  <= p.max_credit_score)
                  AND (p.min_age            IS NULL OR u.age           >= p.min_age)
                  AND (p.max_age            IS NULL OR u.age           <= p.max_age)
                  AND (p.employment_types   IS NULL OR u.employment_status = ANY (p.employment_types)))
                THEN 'fails_hard_criteria'
            WHEN p.other_criteria_text IS NULL THEN 'eligible'
            WHEN p.residual_rules IS NULL THEN 'conditional'
            WHEN NOT (SELECT coalesce(bool_and(CASE
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.monthly_income >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'monthly_income' AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.monthly_income <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.credit_score  >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'credit_score'   AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.credit_score  <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '>=' THEN u.age           >= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        WHEN x->>'field' = 'age'            AND x->>'op' = '<=' THEN u.age           <= (x->>'value')::numeric
                        ELSE true END), true)
                      FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(p.residual_rules, '[]'::jsonb)) AS x
                      WHERE x->>'applies_to' IN ('any', u.employment_status))
                THEN 'not_eligible'
            WHEN jsonb_array_length(p.residual_requirements) > 0 THEN 'conditional'
            ELSE 'eligible' END AS tier
    FROM usr u CROSS JOIN prods p
), naive_kept AS (
    SELECT user_id, product_id, tier FROM naive WHERE tier IN ('eligible', 'conditional')
), optimized AS (  -- what the pipeline stored for this run
    SELECT m.user_id, m.product_id, m.tier
    FROM matches m
    WHERE m.status = 'active' AND m.user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM usr)
      AND m.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM prods)
), diff AS (
    (SELECT * FROM naive_kept EXCEPT SELECT * FROM optimized)
    UNION ALL
    (SELECT * FROM optimized EXCEPT SELECT * FROM naive_kept)
)
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET correctness_ok = ((SELECT count(*) FROM diff) = 0)
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM naive) AS naive_pairs_evaluated,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM naive_kept) AS naive_matches,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM optimized) AS optimized_matches,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM diff) AS mismatches,
    correctness_ok;

UPDATE pipeline_runs SET status = 'done', finished_at = now(),
       rules_compiled = coalesce(rules_compiled, 0), llm_calls = coalesce(llm_calls, 0),
       llm_cache_hits = residual_texts - coalesce(rules_compiled, 0),
       llm_input_tokens = coalesce(llm_input_tokens, 0), llm_output_tokens = coalesce(llm_output_tokens, 0),
       llm_cost_usd_est = coalesce(llm_cost_usd_est, 0)
WHERE run_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING run_id::text, mode, job_id::text, users_in, products_in, naive_pairs, classes,
          class_product_pairs, pairs_after_sql, rule_decided, llm_candidates, not_eligible_pairs,
          residual_texts, rules_compiled, llm_cache_hits, llm_calls, llm_input_tokens, llm_output_tokens,
          llm_cost_usd_est, matches_new, matches_superseded, matches_unchanged, correctness_ok

meta.description: Stage 0 compile criteria (LLM, cached) → Stage 1+2 SQL classes → stats → Stage 3 expand/score/diff → proof.
